gaps.sentence: My grandfather ___ walk five miles to school when he was a boy.
gaps.hint: a past habit no longer true
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' describes past habits or states that are no longer true: used to walk.

gaps.sentence: I ___ the dentist on Thursday afternoon — I booked it last week.
gaps.explanation: A personal arrangement already made takes the present continuous: am seeing.

gaps.sentence: It ___ hard when we left the house, so we took our umbrellas.
gaps.hint: background weather at the moment we left
gaps.explanation: The rain was in progress as a background situation when we left, so the past continuous fits: was raining.

gaps.sentence: She is exhausted because she ___ since dawn.
gaps.hint: since dawn explains her present exhaustion
gaps.explanation: An action running from the past to now and explaining a present state takes the present perfect continuous: has been travelling.

gaps.sentence: Look at the time! We ___ for over two hours.
gaps.hint: for over two hours up to now
gaps.explanation: A duration continuing up to the present moment takes the present perfect continuous: have been chatting.

gaps.sentence: By the time the fire crew arrived, the neighbours ___ the blaze out with buckets of water.
gaps.explanation: The putting out happened before the crew arrived: past perfect 'had put'.

gaps.sentence: I ___ coffee at all, but I drink tea every morning.
gaps.hint: a general habit contrasted with another habit
gaps.explanation: A permanent habit takes the present simple, so the negative form is: don't drink.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ its profits every year since it changed strategy, and analysts expect more growth.
gaps.hint: since clause anchors past to present
gaps.explanation: A 'since' clause connecting a past start to the present requires the present perfect: has increased.
